{{nihongo|'''Kinpu Shrine'''|金峯神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Kinpu Shrine''' (きんぷじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Yoshino, Nara|Q1203731|qid=Q1203731}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nara|af|Nara-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nara|ar|نارا (محافظة)|az|Nara prefekturası|azb|نارا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nara|bat_smg|Naras prefektūra|be|Нара (прэфектура)|bg|Нара (префектура)|bn|নারা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nara|cdo|Nara-gâing|ce|Нара (префектура)|ceb|Nara-ken|ckb|پارێزگای نارا|cs|Prefektura Nara|cy|Nara (talaith)|da|Nara-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nara|eo|Gubernio Nara|es|Prefectura de Nara|et|Nara prefektuur|eu|Nara (prefektura)|fa|استان نارا|fi|Naran prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nara|frr|Nara (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nara|gl|Prefectura de Nara|gor|Prefektur Nara|hak|Nara-yen|he|נארה (מחוז)|hr|Nara (prefektura)|hu|Nara prefektúra|hy|Նարա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nara|ilo|Prepektura ti Nara|it|Prefettura di Nara|ja|奈良県|jv|Préfèktur Nara|ka|ნარის პრეფექტურა|kk|Нара (префектура)|km|ណារ៉ា(ខេត្ត)|ko|나라현|la|Naraënsis|lt|Naros prefektūra|lv|Naras prefektūra|mk|Нара (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯔꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नारा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nara|my|နာရခရိုင်|nl|Nara (prefectuur)|no|Nara (prefektur)|os|Нарæ (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nara|pl|Prefektura Nara|pnb|ضلع نارا|pt|Nara (prefeitura)|ro|Prefectura Nara|ru|Нара (префектура)|sco|Nara Prefectur|sd|نارا پريفيڪچر|se|Nara prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nara|si|නාරා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nara Prefecture|sk|Nara (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nara|sr|Префектура Нара|su|Nara Prefecture|sv|Nara prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nara|ta|நாரா மாநிலம்|tg|Префектураи Нара|th|จังหวัดนาระ|tl|Prepektura ng Nara|tok|ma Nala|tr|Nara (prefektörlük)|tt|Нара (префектура)|uk|Префектура Нара|ur|نارا پریفیکچر|vi|Nara (tỉnh)|war|Nara (prefektura)|wuu|奈良县|zh|奈良县|zh_classical|奈良縣|zh_min_nan|Nara-koān|zh_yue|奈良縣|qid=Q131287}}. It is a shikinaisha (meishin-taisha) and former gosha. Located near Aonegamine at the innermost area of {{ill|Mount Yoshino|Q1036938|qid=Q1036938}}, it enshrines the local tutelary deity of Yoshinoyama.

Its precinct is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property "{{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|Q611345|qid=Q611345}}" (registered July 2004).<ref name="sanken">World Heritage Registration Promotion Council of Three Prefectures (2005), pp.39, 75.</ref>

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|Q4387856|qid=Q4387856|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto}} (main deity), tutelary deity of Yoshinoyama

=== History ===
The foundation is unknown. Since medieval times it has been a site for {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}} practice, and the ''{{ill|Eiga Monogatari|Q1302985|qid=Q1302985}}'' records a visit by {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|Q433133|qid=Q433133}}.

Before the Meiji period, during shinbutsu-shugo, it was called "Konsho Myojin," with associated honji-butsu identified as Akshobhya, Shaka, and Dainichi (Kongokai).

=== Precinct ===
[[File:Konbu Shrine, Yoshino03.JPG|thumb|right|Yoshitsune-kakure-to]]
* Honden
* Haiden - transferred former haiden of {{ill|Yoshino Shrine|Q11414497|qid=Q11414497}}
* Yoshitsune Hidden Tower (also called Kenuke-no-to) - rebuilt in early Taisho period; linked to legend of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|Q310445|qid=Q310445}}

=== Cultural properties ===
=== National Treasure ===
[[ファイル:Gilt-bronze Fujiwara no Michinaga sutra case (Kinpu Shrine, Yoshino-gun, Nara Prefecture).jpg|thumb|150px|Gilt-bronze sutra tube of Fujiwara no Michinaga (1007), National Treasure]]
* Gilt-bronze Fujiwara no Michinaga sutra tube (1)
: Designated National Treasure (archaeological material) on November 22, 1952. One of the Kinpusan sutra-mound finds; inscription includes date "August 11, 1007."
: Height 35.8 cm, mouth diameter 15.7 cm. A large thick cylindrical copper tube with gilding, engraved with 510 characters in 24 lines explaining the motive and process of sutra burial. It is one of the oldest securely dated sutra-mound artifacts and aligns with records in Michinaga's diary ''Mido Kanpakuki''. Deposited in the Kyoto National Museum.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Excavated objects from Kinpusan sutra mound in Yamato Province
: Group designation (8 categories) as Important Cultural Property in 1953, with additions in 1955, including a silver-plated sutra box, remains of a gilt-bronze stand, and multiple fragments of gold-lettered sutras on indigo paper.
* Iron tsuba with stupa-openwork design (with maki-e box)
: Designated Important Cultural Property (craft) in 1925.

=== Historic site ===
* {{ill|Ōmine Okugakemichi|Q11434795|qid=Q11434795}}
: The shrine precinct is part of this nationally designated historic site (designated December 19, 2002).<ref name="Bunka"/>

=== Access ===
From Kintetsu Yoshino Line {{ill|Yoshino Station (Nara)|Q8056197|qid=Q8056197|lt=Yoshino Station}}, transfer to the Yoshino Ropeway to "Yoshinoyama," then about 1 hour 45 minutes on foot; or bus from Yoshinoyama Station to "Okusenbon-guchi" (about 23 minutes), then 5 minutes on foot.
